# SmartAttend Privacy Policy

**Status: draft, not legal advice.** This document was generated by auditing what the SmartAttend codebase actually collects, stores, and transmits, as of the date below — it accurately describes the *system*, but it is not a substitute for review by your institution's data protection officer or qualified legal counsel before this is published to real students. Biometric data specifically is treated as sensitive/special-category personal data under most data protection frameworks, including Nigeria's — do not go live without that review.

*Last audited: 2026-09-04. Applies to: SmartAttend as implemented in this repository.*

## 1. Who this covers

SmartAttend is operated by **[Institution name — fill in]** ("we", "us") for **[course/department/faculty — fill in]** at the University of Cross River State. This policy covers students, lecturers, and administrators who use the SmartAttend web application to register, sign in, or record and review class attendance.

## 2. What we collect, and why

This section is drawn directly from the application's database schema and code — every field listed here is something the running system actually stores or transmits, not a generic template list.

### 2.1 Account and identity data
| Data | Who it's collected from | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Full name, email address | Everyone (students, lecturers, admins) | Identify your account, sign you in, address you by name in the interface. |
| Password | Everyone | Sign-in. **Never stored in plain text** — hashed with Argon2 before it touches the database; even we cannot read it back. |
| Matric number, department, academic level | Students | Tie an attendance record to a specific enrolled student, matching institutional records. |
| Role (student / lecturer / admin) | Everyone | Determines what you can see and do in the system. |

### 2.2 Biometric data — face verification
This is the most sensitive category SmartAttend handles, and it gets the most careful treatment in the system:

- When you enrol (self-registration or admin enrolment) or check in to a class, your device's camera captures a photo or a short pair of frames.
- That image is sent, over your session's encrypted connection, to a dedicated verification service that detects your face and computes a **mathematical representation of it** (a 128-number "embedding") — a one-way transformation that cannot be reversed back into a photo of your face.
- **The photo itself is never saved.** It exists only in server memory for the moment it takes to compute the embedding, then it is discarded. Only the embedding — the numbers — is stored against your student record, to be compared against future check-in attempts.
- At check-in, two freshly captured frames are compared against each other (to confirm they aren't a single static photo replayed twice) and against your stored embedding (to confirm identity). Neither frame is stored either way, pass or fail — only the numeric result (matched/not matched, a confidence score) is recorded.
- **What we do not do:** we do not run facial recognition against any database except your own enrolled embedding; we do not share biometric data with any third party; we do not use it for anything other than attendance verification.

### 2.3 Attendance activity
| Data | Why |
|---|---|
| Check-in timestamp, course, session | The actual attendance record — this is the product's purpose. |
| Face-match confidence score | Lets a lecturer review borderline or flagged attempts. |
| Failed/flagged attempt records (a mismatch or a check-in that failed the liveness check) | Kept separately from successful attendance, visible to the lecturer of that class, so a genuine student who was wrongly rejected can be manually reviewed rather than losing their attendance record with no recourse. |

### 2.4 Session and technical data
| Data | Why | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in tokens (access + refresh) | Keep you signed in without retyping your password on every action. | Your browser's session storage (cleared when you sign out or close the browser tab's session) and, for refresh tokens, a hashed record server-side so a stolen token can be revoked. |
| IP address | Used momentarily to enforce rate limits (e.g., blocking repeated failed login attempts) on the request itself. | Not written to any database table — used in memory for that one request's rate-limit check, then discarded. |
| Course schedule, class roster, registration-approval history (who approved/rejected a request, when, and why) | Operating the system — scheduling, course enrolment, and the admin approval queue for new student accounts. | Application database. |

### 2.5 What we deliberately do not collect
- We do not run advertising or analytics trackers of any kind.
- We do not collect your location.
- We do not access your device's camera roll or files — only a live camera frame you actively capture.
- We do not sell, rent, or share your personal or biometric data with any third party for marketing or any other purpose.

## 3. Third parties involved

- **Google Fonts** (fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com): the interface's typefaces load from Google's font service. Loading a font file means your browser makes a request to Google, which — like any web request — includes your IP address. Google's own privacy policy governs that request; we do not pass any SmartAttend account data to Google.
- **No other third party ever receives your data.** The face-verification service, the database, and the application server are all operated as part of this same system, not handed off to an external vendor.

## 4. Who can see your data

Access is role-restricted in the application itself, not just a policy promise:

- **You** can always see your own profile and your own attendance history.
- **Lecturers** can see the roster and attendance records for courses they teach — not other lecturers' courses, not students outside their own classes.
- **Administrators** can see system-wide account and attendance data, and review pending self-registration requests, as part of operating the system.
- Biometric embeddings are never displayed to anyone, including administrators — they exist only as an input to the automated face-match comparison.

## 5. How long we keep it

**Being direct about a real limitation:** as implemented today, SmartAttend does not have an automatic data-deletion or retention-expiry feature — records persist until someone with database access removes them. If your institution adopts this system for real use, it should define and operationally enforce a retention period (for example: biometric templates and attendance records deleted a set period after a student graduates or withdraws) — this policy will be updated once that's decided, and **[Institution name]** commits to stating that period here rather than leaving it open-ended.

## 6. Your rights

Depending on your institution's data protection obligations (in Nigeria, the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023), you generally have the right to:
- Ask what personal data we hold about you and receive a copy of it.
- Ask us to correct inaccurate data (e.g., a misspelled name or wrong department).
- Withdraw biometric consent — noting that since face verification is one half of SmartAttend's "double-lock" mechanism, withdrawing it means falling back to whatever manual attendance process your institution maintains alongside it, not automatic check-in.
- Ask about or object to how your data is used, and raise a complaint with your institution's data protection officer or the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.

**Contact for privacy requests:** **[email/office — fill in before publishing]**.

## 7. Security measures in place

- Passwords are hashed with Argon2, never stored or logged in plain text.
- Sign-in tokens are short-lived (15-minute access tokens) with longer-lived refresh tokens that rotate on use and can be individually revoked (e.g., on logout, or if a device is lost).
- The QR code used for classroom check-in is cryptographically signed and expires every 30 seconds, so a photographed or shared code stops working almost immediately.
- Face verification runs entirely on the server; a device's camera feed is never trusted at face value; a stolen embedding array cannot be replayed by a script the way it could in an earlier version of this system.
- Production deployments are required to use real, random secret keys and HTTPS — the system refuses to start with placeholder development secrets outside of an explicit local-development mode.

## 8. Changes to this policy

We'll update this document when what the system actually does changes, and note the date at the top. Continued use of SmartAttend after an update means you've had the chance to review the change.
